3	-- ============================================================
4	-- Sprint 1: Foundation schema — topics, bots, bindings, channels, identities
5	-- ============================================================
6	
7	-- 1. Topics — the central organizing concept for all artifacts
8	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS topics (
9	    id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
10	    slug text NOT NULL UNIQUE,
11	    display_name text NOT NULL,
12	    description text NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
13	    participants_shape text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'dyad' CHECK (participants_shape IN ('dyad', 'solo', 'group')),
14	    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
15	);
16	
17	-- 2. Bots — intentionally thin; scope/version fields live in code per §3
18	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bots (
19	    id text PRIMARY KEY,
20	    display_name text NOT NULL,
21	    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
22	);
23	
24	-- 3. Dyads — a single row per relationship pair
25	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dyads (
26	    id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
27	    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
28	);
29	
30	-- 4. Dyad members — links users to their dyad
31	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS dyad_members (
32	    dyad_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES dyads(id),
33	    user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
34	    joined_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
35	    PRIMARY KEY (dyad_id, user_id)
36	);
37	
38	-- 5. Bot bindings — which bots are bound to which dyads/users
39	-- XOR: exactly one of dyad_id or user_id must be non-null
40	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS bot_bindings (
41	    id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
42	    bot_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES bots(id),
43	    dyad_id uuid REFERENCES dyads(id),
44	    user_id uuid REFERENCES users(id),
45	    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
46	    CONSTRAINT bot_bindings_xor CHECK ((user_id IS NOT NULL) <> (dyad_id IS NOT NULL))
47	);
48	
49	-- 6. Channels — transport-specific addresses where bots listen
50	-- Two uniqueness mechanisms:
51	--   (a) raw-column UNIQUE for standard direct-match lookups
52	--   (b) expression index for COALESCE'd ON CONFLICT used by seed_channels.py
53	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS channels (
54	    id uuid PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
55	    bot_id text NOT NULL REFERENCES bots(id),
56	    transport text NOT NULL CHECK (transport IN ('discord', 'whatsapp', 'sms', 'web')),
57	    address text NOT NULL,
58	    guild_id text,
59	    channel_id text,
60	    config jsonb NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}'::jsonb,
61	    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
62	    UNIQUE (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)
63	);
64	
65	-- Expression-based unique index: COALESCE treats NULL guild_id/channel_id as empty string,
66	-- allowing seed_channels.py to use ON CONFLICT (transport, address, COALESCE(guild_id,''), COALESCE(channel_id,''))
67	-- Without this index, the expression-based ON CONFLICT target would fail with
68	-- 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the on conflict specification'.
69	CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS channels_uniq_coalesced
70	    ON channels (transport, address, COALESCE(guild_id, ''), COALESCE(channel_id, ''));
71	
72	-- 7. User identities — maps transport+address pairs to user records
73	-- verified_at is nullable; account-linking workflows fill it in S4+
74	CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS user_identities (
75	    transport text NOT NULL CHECK (transport IN ('discord', 'whatsapp', 'sms', 'legacy')),
76	    address text NOT NULL,
77	    user_id uuid NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id),
78	    verified_at timestamptz,
79	    created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now(),
80	    PRIMARY KEY (transport, address)
81	);

98	-- Uses an existence-check DO block rather than ON CONFLICT on a random PK
99	-- so that re-running the migration is a true no-op.
100	DO $$
101	DECLARE
102	    _dyad_id uuid;
103	    _user_a_id uuid;
104	    _user_b_id uuid;
105	BEGIN
106	    -- Check if any dyad already has a binding for mediator
107	    PERFORM 1 FROM bot_bindings WHERE bot_id = 'mediator' AND dyad_id IS NOT NULL;
108	    IF FOUND THEN
109	        RETURN;
110	    END IF;
111	
112	    -- Find two users to form the dyad
113	    SELECT id INTO _user_a_id FROM users ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1;
114	    SELECT id INTO _user_b_id FROM users WHERE id <> _user_a_id ORDER BY created_at LIMIT 1;
115	
116	    IF _user_a_id IS NULL OR _user_b_id IS NULL THEN
117	        -- Not enough users — skip dyad creation; seed_channels.sql populates identities
118	        -- and dyad can be formed later
119	        RETURN;
120	    END IF;
121	
122	    -- Create dyad
123	    INSERT INTO dyads DEFAULT VALUES RETURNING id INTO _dyad_id;
124	
125	    -- Add members
126	    INSERT INTO dyad_members (dyad_id, user_id) VALUES (_dyad_id, _user_a_id);
127	    INSERT INTO dyad_members (dyad_id, user_id) VALUES (_dyad_id, _user_b_id);
128	
129	    -- Create bot binding for mediator to this dyad
130	    INSERT INTO bot_bindings (bot_id, dyad_id) VALUES ('mediator', _dyad_id);
131	END $$;
132	
133	-- ============================================================
134	-- Backfill user_identities from users.phone
135	-- transport='legacy' per locked decision §16.8 (all existing rows).
136	-- ============================================================
137	INSERT INTO user_identities (transport, address, user_id)
138	SELECT 'legacy', phone, id
139	FROM users
140	WHERE phone IS NOT NULL

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	"""Artifact-read lint — flags direct ``FROM <artifact_table>`` reads that are
3	not scoped through ``artifact_topics``.
4	
5	Scans ``app/`` for the regex ``\\bFROM\\s+(memories|themes|observations|
6	watch_items|distillations|out_of_bounds)\\b``.  Every hit must have the
7	enclosing SQL string contain ``join_artifact_topics`` (the helper call that
8	emits the JOIN fragment), or be in the explicit whitelist.
9	
10	Design notes
11	------------
12	* FROM-only design: UPDATE statements are NOT checked (deferred to S6).
13	* ``FROM artifact_topics`` is intentionally NOT in the regex alternation
14	  because it is the bridge table itself, not an artifact table.
15	* S6 TODO: add UPDATE checking.
16	* We detect compliance via ``join_artifact_topics`` in the source rather than
17	  ``_at_`` in runtime SQL because f-string interpolations don't expand at
18	  scan time.
19	
20	Usage:
21	    python scripts/lint_artifact_reads.py           # scan app/ directory
22	    python scripts/lint_artifact_reads.py --help    # show this message
23	    python scripts/lint_artifact_reads.py --dir app # specify scan directory
24	"""
25	
26	from __future__ import annotations
27	
28	import argparse
29	import re
30	import sys
31	from pathlib import Path
32	
33	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
34	# The regex: FROM {memories, themes, observations, watch_items, distillations,
35	# out_of_bounds} — captures the table name.
36	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
37	_FROM_ARTIFACT_RE = re.compile(
38	    r"\bFROM\s+(memories|themes|observations|watch_items|distillations|out_of_bounds)\b",
39	    re.IGNORECASE,
40	)

{
  "file_path": "/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/Veas/scripts/check_per_bot_panels.py",
  "content": "#!/usr/bin/env python3\n\"\"\"Observability sanity: group turn_audit_events and tool_calls by bot_id.\n\nS2a added per-bot split panes; this script is the code-level check that the\npanels still render correctly for a second (staging-only) bot. It connects to\nDATABASE_URL with statement_cache_size=0 (Supabase pooler is transaction-mode\non port 6543, see S1 lesson #3) and prints two tables: events grouped by\nbot_id and tool_calls grouped by bot_id, both windowed over a recent\ninterval.\n\nUsage:\n    python scripts/check_per_bot_panels.py --help\n    python scripts/check_per_bot_panels.py --hours 24\n    python scripts/check_per_bot_panels.py --bot-id mediator --hours 6\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport argparse\nimport asyncio\nimport os\nimport sys\nfrom typing import Any\n\n\ndef _parse_args(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> argparse.Namespace:\n    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(\n        description=\"Group turn_audit_events and tool_calls by bot_id for per-bot panel sanity.\",\n    )\n    parser.add_argument(\"--hours\", type=int, default=24, help=\"window in hours (default: 24)\")\n    parser.add_argument(\"--bot-id\", type=str, default=None, help=\"optional bot_id filter\")\n    parser.add_argument(\n        \"--database-url\",\n        type=str,\n        default=os.environ.get(\"DATABASE_URL\"),\n        help=\"DATABASE_URL override (default: $DATABASE_URL)\",\n    )\n    return parser.parse_args(argv)\n\n\nasync def _run(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    if not args.database_url:\n        print(\"error: DATABASE_URL is not set\", file=sys.stderr)\n        return 2\n\n    import asyncpg  # local import so --help works without the dep installed\n\n    # Supabase pooler is transaction-mode on port 6543 — see S1 lesson #3.\n    pool = await asyncpg.create_pool(args.database_url, statement_cache_size=0)\n    try:\n        bot_filter = \"AND bot_id = $2\" if args.bot_id else \"\"\n        params: list[Any] = [args.hours]\n        if args.bot_id:\n            params.append(args.bot_id)\n\n        events = await pool.fetch(\n            f\"\"\"\n            SELECT COALESCE(bot_id, '<null>') AS bot_id, COUNT(*) AS event_count\n            FROM turn_audit_events\n            WHERE occurred_at >= now() - ($1 || ' hours')::interval\n              {bot_filter}\n            GROUP BY 1\n            ORDER BY 1\n            \"\"\",\n            *params,\n        )\n        tool_calls = await pool.fetch(\n            f\"\"\"\n            SELECT COALESCE(bot_id, '<null>') AS bot_id, COUNT(*) AS call_count\n            FROM tool_calls\n            WHERE called_at >= now() - ($1 || ' hours')::interval\n              {bot_filter}\n            GROUP BY 1\n            ORDER BY 1\n            \"\"\",\n            *params,\n        )\n    finally:\n        await pool.close()\n\n    print(f\"turn_audit_events (last {args.hours}h) by bot_id:\")\n    for row in events:\n        print(f\"  {row['bot_id']:<24} {row['event_count']}\")\n    print()\n    print(f\"tool_calls (last {args.hours}h) by bot_id:\")\n    for row in tool_calls:\n        print(f\"  {row['bot_id']:<24} {row['call_count']}\")\n    return 0\n\n\ndef main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:\n    args = _parse_args(argv)\n    return asyncio.run(_run(args))\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    sys.exit(main())\n"
}

Opus 4.7 across all phases.

**Locked decisions (do not relitigate during plan/critique):**

## Sprint 4 — §16.5 verbatim

**Goal.** Authorization layer (§6, §8) and `topic_status` (§7) ship. `consult_perspective` rewritten to actually clone. **Solo bot infrastructure pre-flighted in parallel** so S5 is pure code work.

This is a heavier sprint than earlier drafts implied — 19 read-phase tools plus read surfaces hiding in `write_tools.py` (`list_scheduled_tasks`, etc.) all get `scope` parameter changes, and tool-schema changes are model-behavior risk.

**Pre-flight context.**

- Lock decision A (peek window): default 14d. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision D (status cap N): default 5 most-recently-active topics per user. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision B: status update folded into `record` step, per §7.5. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision: which solo bot is #2 — coach, career topic, Discord transport. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision C (solo crisis default): refer to dyadic bot + external resources. ✓ Locked above.
- Read `consult_perspective.py:105-139` — the current code reconstructs `TurnContext` field-by-field, it does not clone. Plan a `dataclasses.replace` helper.
- Audit the read-phase tool registry (`tools/registry.py:157`) — count is ~19. Catalogue which need a `scope` arg vs which are scope-irrelevant (`get_bot_actions`, `recent_activity`, etc.).

**Work items, ordered (authorization track).**

1. `ReadScopes`/`WriteScopes` enforcement: every read tool consults `ctx.read_scopes`; every write consults `ctx.write_scopes`. Add `scope` parameter to artifact-reading tools only (skip scope-irrelevant tools). With one topic, `"own"` and `"all"` resolve the same — verify plumbing without changing output.
2. **`consult_perspective` rewrite**: replace the field-by-field `TurnContext` reconstruction at `consult_perspective.py:105` with a `dataclasses.replace(ctx, …)` helper. Add a unit test that enumerates every `TurnContext` field and asserts none are dropped on clone. Add a lint that fails if any new `TurnContext(...)` constructor appears outside the clone helper.
3. `set_topic_status` tool. Register only for `mediator` initially. Folded into `record` step instruction. Enforce headline ≤ 80 chars, body ≤ 300 chars.
4. Hot context: status block (own topic) for served user(s) + pair (`dyad_id` set, `user_id` NULL). Policy-gated cross-topic status injection — code path live but with one topic emits nothing.

7. Lint/test: every DB-touching function in `read_tools.py`/`write_tools.py` accepts and uses `ctx`.

**Mid-sprint checkpoint.**

- A no-op second `BotSpec` in a test (`read_scopes.topics={"career"}`) fails to read `relationship` artifacts.
- Solo bot transport reachable in staging; webhook resolves to the right `bot_id`; OOB guardrail fires.

**Definition of done.**

- Mediator writes status; status block renders.
- Negative-permission test in CI passes.
- Solo bot transport, channel, secrets, consent are all green in staging (or explicit TODO if blocked).

**Risks.**

- `scope` parameter on every artifact-reading tool changes tool schemas → may affect mediator. The undocumented-first rollout strategy mitigates.
- Status injection token budget. Enforce headline ≤ 80, body ≤ 300 in `set_topic_status`.
- `consult_perspective` is the easiest leak path — the enumeration test is MANDATORY.
- Solo pre-flight runs in parallel; if it blocks (e.g. Discord bot account approval delays), defer those items to S5 with explicit TODOs but DON'T expand S5 by more than ~3 days.

**Deliberately not in this sprint.**

Multi-topic writes via `topic_slugs`. Solo bot prompt or hot context code (lands in S5). Account-linking workflow. PROD promotion of the solo bot (S5).

## S1-S3 lessons the executor must honor

1. **CLI scripts**: invoke with `--help` to confirm parseable.
2. **SQL fragments in Python strings**: dry-run via `EXPLAIN` or sanity-check types (no `max(uuid)` etc.).
3. **asyncpg pool against `DATABASE_URL`**: pass `statement_cache_size=0` (Supabase port 6543 is transaction-mode).
4. **No `hash()` for deterministic IDs** — use `hashlib.sha1`.
5. **Schema filters in validation queries** use `'mediator'` not `'public'`.
6. **For psql migrations against Supabase**: use port 5432 session-mode for DDL.
7. **Don't introduce scope creep**: no unrelated features or unused fields in shared classes.
8. **NO defensive fallbacks**: per S3 lesson, don't add `topic_id IS NULL` or similar permissive filters.
9. **For verify-human-heavy plans**: keep criterion count manageable (~10-15); each criterion should be cheaply auto-verifiable from artifacts.
10. **S3 cutover is committed**: every artifact read goes through `topic_filter.join_artifact_topics()`. New code follows this pattern, don't reintroduce direct reads.
11. **Pytest baseline**: 534 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on s3-join-cutover HEAD. S4 must maintain or improve.

- Solo bot infra accidentally touches prod (any non-staging DB write) — STOP, revert.
- Negative-permission test (career-scoped bot trying to read relationship artifacts) PASSES (it should FAIL — that's the point) — STOP, fix authorization layer.

- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan’s `scripts/seed_channels.py` uses `on conflict (transport, address, coalesce(guild_id,''), coalesce(channel_id,'')) do nothing`, but the 0020 migration defines the table with a standard `unique (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)` constraint on raw columns. postgresql `on conflict` target lists must reference the exact column names of a unique constraint or a matching unique index; expression constructs like `coalesce` in the target list do not match a raw-column unique constraint and will raise a syntax or 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the on conflict specification' error at runtime. the seed script will fail unless either (a) the table is changed to use an expression-based unique index with those exact coalesce expressions, or (b) the seed script is rewritten to query-first/insert-if-missing or uses the plain column names and accepts the null-handling semantics of the constraint. async def log_feedback(ctx: TurnContext, args: LogFeedbackInput) -> LogFeedbackOutput:
    started = _start()
    row = await ctx.pool.fetchrow(
        """
        INSERT INTO feedback (from_user_id, target_type, target_id, sentiment, content, source, bot_id, topic_id)
        VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, $8)
        RETURNING id
        """,
        args.from_user_id,
        args.target_type,
        args.target_id,
        args.sentiment.value,
        args.content,
        args.source,
        ctx.bot_id,
        ctx.primary_topic_id,
    )
    result = LogFeedbackOutput(id=row["id"])
    await _log_tool_call(ctx, "log_feedback", args, started, result)
    return result

## S1-S3 lessons the executor must honor

1. **CLI scripts**: invoke with `--help` to confirm parseable.
2. **SQL fragments in Python strings**: dry-run via `EXPLAIN` or sanity-check types (no `max(uuid)` etc.).
3. **asyncpg pool against `DATABASE_URL`**: pass `statement_cache_size=0` (Supabase port 6543 is transaction-mode).
4. **No `hash()` for deterministic IDs** — use `hashlib.sha1`.
5. **Schema filters in validation queries** use `'mediator'` not `'public'`.
6. **For psql migrations against Supabase**: use port 5432 session-mode for DDL.
7. **Don't introduce scope creep**: no unrelated features or unused fields in shared classes.
8. **NO defensive fallbacks**: per S3 lesson, don't add `topic_id IS NULL` or similar permissive filters.
9. **For verify-human-heavy plans**: keep criterion count manageable (~10-15); each criterion should be cheaply auto-verifiable from artifacts.
10. **S3 cutover is committed**: every artifact read goes through `topic_filter.join_artifact_topics()`. New code follows this pattern, don't reintroduce direct reads.
11. **Pytest baseline**: 534 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on s3-join-cutover HEAD. S4 must maintain or improve.

## Stop conditions

- Any test that was passing on `s3-join-cutover` HEAD (commit 52d6dab) starts failing — STOP, report.
- `consult_perspective` enumeration test fails to enumerate any field — STOP, fix (this is a real correctness gap).
- Tool-schema changes break mediator behavior in eval (if eval suite available) — STOP, audit.
- Solo bot infra accidentally touches prod (any non-staging DB write) — STOP, revert.
- Negative-permission test (career-scoped bot trying to read relationship artifacts) PASSES (it should FAIL — that's the point) — STOP, fix authorization layer.

- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan’s `scripts/seed_channels.py` uses `on conflict (transport, address, coalesce(guild_id,''), coalesce(channel_id,'')) do nothing`, but the 0020 migration defines the table with a standard `unique (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)` constraint on raw columns. postgresql `on conflict` target lists must reference the exact column names of a unique constraint or a matching unique index; expression constructs like `coalesce` in the target list do not match a raw-column unique constraint and will raise a syntax or 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the on conflict specification' error at runtime. the seed script will fail unless either (a) the table is changed to use an expression-based unique index with those exact coalesce expressions, or (b) the seed script is rewritten to query-first/insert-if-missing or uses the plain column names and accepts the null-handling semantics of the constraint. 49	        )
50	        return

54	            "keeping module-level defaults"

61	
62	    rebuilt = MediatorBotSpec(

77	    )

Else deny.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nfrom typing import Any\n\n# Artifact-reading tools that take a `scope` parameter (10 tools).\nARTIFACT_READ_TOOLS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({\n    \"get_memories\",\n    \"get_observations\",\n    \"get_distillations\",\n    \"get_oob\",\n    \"summarize_oob_topics\",\n    \"list_themes\",\n    \"get_theme\",\n    \"list_watch_items\",\n    \"list_bridge_candidates\",\n    \"get_self_model\",\n})\n\n# Artifact-writing tools that consult ctx.write_scopes (21 tools).\n# NB: transport (send/edit/delete/react), scheduling, log_feedback, escalate,\n# and read-shaped tools are intentionally NOT in this set.\nARTIFACT_WRITE_TOOLS: frozenset[str] = frozenset({\n    \"update_user_style_notes\",\n    \"update_cross_thread_sharing_default\",\n    \"create_bridge_candidate\",\n    \"update_bridge_candidate\",\n    \"send_bridge_candidate\",\n    \"add_memory\",\n    \"update_memory\",\n    \"supersede_memory\",\n    \"create_theme\",\n    \"update_theme\",\n    \"add_watch_item\",\n    \"update_watch_item\",\n    \"address_watch_item\",\n    \"log_observation\",\n    \"update_observation\",\n    \"add_distillation\",\n    \"update_distillation\",\n    \"revise_distillation\",\n    \"add_oob\",\n    \"update_oob\",\n    \"lift_oob\",\n})\n\n\ndef _resolve_target(requested_scope: str, primary_topic_slug: str | None) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Resolve 'own' to ctx.primary_topic_slug; pass through anything else.\"\"\"\n    if requested_scope == \"own\":\n        return primary_topic_slug\n    return requested_scope\n\n\ndef check_read_scope(ctx: Any, requested_scope: str = \"own\") -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return None when the read is allowed; an error string when denied.\n\n    None-permissive when ctx.read_scopes is None.\n    \"\"\"\n    scopes = getattr(ctx, \"read_scopes\", None)\n    if scopes is None:\n        return None\n    topics = scopes.topics\n    if \"all\" in topics:\n        return None\n    target = _resolve_target(requested_scope, getattr(ctx, \"primary_topic_slug\", None))\n    if target is None:\n        return f\"scope_denied: read scope='{requested_scope}' unresolved (no primary_topic_slug)\"\n    if \"own\" in topics and target == getattr(ctx, \"primary_topic_slug\", None):\n        return None\n    if target in topics:\n        return None\n    return (\n        f\"scope_denied: read scope='{requested_scope}' not in {sorted(topics)} \"\n        f\"(primary={getattr(ctx, 'primary_topic_slug', None)})\"\n    )\n\n\ndef check_write_scope(ctx: Any) -> str | None:\n    \"\"\"Return None when the write is allowed; an error string when denied.\n\n    The write-scope gate currently authorizes against the bot's primary topic\n    (ctx.primary_topic_slug). Multi-topic writes are S6.\n\n    None-permissive when ctx.write_scopes is None.\n    \"\"\"\n    scopes = getattr(ctx, \"write_scopes\", None)\n    if scopes is None:\n        return None\n    topics = scopes.topics\n    if \"all\" in topics:\n        return None\n    primary = getattr(ctx, \"primary_topic_slug\", None)\n    if \"own\" in topics and primary is not None:\n        return None\n    if primary is not None and primary in topics:\n        return None\n    return (\n        f\"write_scope_denied: primary='{primary}' not in {sorted(topics)}\"\n    )\n"

- Audit the read-phase tool registry (`tools/registry.py:157`) — count is ~19. Catalogue which need a `scope` arg vs which are scope-irrelevant (`get_bot_actions`, `recent_activity`, etc.).

**Work items, ordered (authorization track).**

1. `ReadScopes`/`WriteScopes` enforcement: every read tool consults `ctx.read_scopes`; every write consults `ctx.write_scopes`. Add `scope` parameter to artifact-reading tools only (skip scope-irrelevant tools). With one topic, `"own"` and `"all"` resolve the same — verify plumbing without changing output.
2. **`consult_perspective` rewrite**: replace the field-by-field `TurnContext` reconstruction at `consult_perspective.py:105` with a `dataclasses.replace(ctx, …)` helper. Add a unit test that enumerates every `TurnContext` field and asserts none are dropped on clone. Add a lint that fails if any new `TurnContext(...)` constructor appears outside the clone helper.
3. `set_topic_status` tool. Register only for `mediator` initially. Folded into `record` step instruction. Enforce headline ≤ 80 chars, body ≤ 300 chars.
4. Hot context: status block (own topic) for served user(s) + pair (`dyad_id` set, `user_id` NULL). Policy-gated cross-topic status injection — code path live but with one topic emits nothing.
5. Cross-topic peek block code path — same: code path live, emits nothing with one topic.
6. Mediator's BotSpec: `cross_topic_policy = "peek"`, `read_scopes = ReadScopes(topics={"own"}, allow_cross_topic_peek=True, allow_cross_topic_status_injection=True)`, `write_scopes = WriteScopes(topics={"relationship"}, require_reason_for_cross_topic=True)`.
7. Lint/test: every DB-touching function in `read_tools.py`/`write_tools.py` accepts and uses `ctx`.
8. **Tool-schema rollout strategy**: ship `scope` parameter undocumented in tool descriptions for one deploy, observe no behavior regression in evals, then surface in descriptions in a follow-up deploy. THIS SPRINT outputs the undocumented form.
9. Per-(user, bot) pause WRITE path (read path landed in S2a): admin endpoint + tool, defaulting to off.

**Work items, in parallel (solo pre-flight track) — STAGING ONLY.**

10. Provision the solo "coach" bot's transport in STAGING: new Discord bot account.
11. Create `channels`/`bots`/`topics`/`bot_bindings` rows for the solo bot in **staging only** — not prod yet. Add a migration if needed (e.g. `0031_coach_staging_seed.sql`); only applies to staging.

15. Observability dashboards: confirm the per-bot split panes built in S2a render correctly for a second (staging-only) bot. — Code-level check is sufficient; do not require actual Grafana access.

**Mid-sprint checkpoint.**

- Mediator running with authorization wired. Pytest 534+ pass.
- A no-op second `BotSpec` in a test (`read_scopes.topics={"career"}`) fails to read `relationship` artifacts.
- Solo bot transport reachable in staging; webhook resolves to the right `bot_id`; OOB guardrail fires.

**Definition of done.**

- Every artifact read/write checks `ctx.read_scopes`/`ctx.write_scopes`. `consult_perspective` cloning verified by enumeration test.
- Mediator writes status; status block renders.
- Negative-permission test in CI passes.
- Solo bot transport, channel, secrets, consent are all green in staging (or explicit TODO if blocked).

**Risks.**

- `scope` parameter on every artifact-reading tool changes tool schemas → may affect mediator. The undocumented-first rollout strategy mitigates.
- Status injection token budget. Enforce headline ≤ 80, body ≤ 300 in `set_topic_status`.
- `consult_perspective` is the easiest leak path — the enumeration test is MANDATORY.
- Solo pre-flight runs in parallel; if it blocks (e.g. Discord bot account approval delays), defer those items to S5 with explicit TODOs but DON'T expand S5 by more than ~3 days.

**Deliberately not in this sprint.**

Multi-topic writes via `topic_slugs`. Solo bot prompt or hot context code (lands in S5). Account-linking workflow. PROD promotion of the solo bot (S5).

## S1-S3 lessons the executor must honor

1. **CLI scripts**: invoke with `--help` to confirm parseable.
2. **SQL fragments in Python strings**: dry-run via `EXPLAIN` or sanity-check types (no `max(uuid)` etc.).
3. **asyncpg pool against `DATABASE_URL`**: pass `statement_cache_size=0` (Supabase port 6543 is transaction-mode).
4. **No `hash()` for deterministic IDs** — use `hashlib.sha1`.
5. **Schema filters in validation queries** use `'mediator'` not `'public'`.
6. **For psql migrations against Supabase**: use port 5432 session-mode for DDL.
7. **Don't introduce scope creep**: no unrelated features or unused fields in shared classes.
8. **NO defensive fallbacks**: per S3 lesson, don't add `topic_id IS NULL` or similar permissive filters.
9. **For verify-human-heavy plans**: keep criterion count manageable (~10-15); each criterion should be cheaply auto-verifiable from artifacts.
10. **S3 cutover is committed**: every artifact read goes through `topic_filter.join_artifact_topics()`. New code follows this pattern, don't reintroduce direct reads.
11. **Pytest baseline**: 534 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on s3-join-cutover HEAD. S4 must maintain or improve.

- Any test that was passing on `s3-join-cutover` HEAD (commit 52d6dab) starts failing — STOP, report.
- `consult_perspective` enumeration test fails to enumerate any field — STOP, fix (this is a real correctness gap).
- Tool-schema changes break mediator behavior in eval (if eval suite available) — STOP, audit.
- Solo bot infra accidentally touches prod (any non-staging DB write) — STOP, revert.
- Negative-permission test (career-scoped bot trying to read relationship artifacts) PASSES (it should FAIL — that's the point) — STOP, fix authorization layer.

        Debt watch items (do not make these worse):
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan’s `scripts/seed_channels.py` uses `on conflict (transport, address, coalesce(guild_id,''), coalesce(channel_id,'')) do nothing`, but the 0020 migration defines the table with a standard `unique (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)` constraint on raw columns. postgresql `on conflict` target lists must reference the exact column names of a unique constraint or a matching unique index; expression constructs like `coalesce` in the target list do not match a raw-column unique constraint and will raise a syntax or 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the on conflict specification' error at runtime. the seed script will fail unless either (a) the table is changed to use an expression-based unique index with those exact coalesce expressions, or (b) the seed script is rewritten to query-first/insert-if-missing or uses the plain column names and accepts the null-handling semantics of the constraint. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: phase b cte pair (`ins` and `src`) requires identical where/order/limit clauses for cursor correctness. both are written aligned but nothing enforces the invariant during executor edits; drift would silently mis-advance cursor. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: step 5.1 says `dyad_id` is appended `before the existing-fields preserved block beginning at line 34`. actual line 34 in turn_context.py is a blank/comment line followed by `current_step: turnstep = "respond"` at the next line. placement intent is clear (append at end of optional block), but the line reference may drift after the field is added. minor precision wobble; not a blocker. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: eval baseline capture (step 2) is technically blocked by infra. the plan's approach (write script in main tree, copy to worktree, run there) assumes `python scripts/capture_eval_baseline.py` can connect to the supabase pooler. per user note, the pooler's transaction-mode does not preserve `set search_path` across connection acquisitions, so the script would fail with schema lookup errors. the plan should add an alternative path (port 5432 session-mode override, or explicit schema-qualified queries everywhere, or defer entirely). (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the lint script `scripts/lint_inserts.py` has a directory-not-found error path at lines 305-309 that still exits 0. the plan step 13 says to remove the `# todo(s2b)` marker at line 308 but does not mention changing the `sys.exit(0)` at line 309 to a non-zero exit code. after the script is flipped to blocking mode, invoking it with an invalid `--dir` argument (or when `args.dir` resolves to a non-existent path) will silently exit 0. this defeats the ci-blocking intent because a typo in the scan directory would be treated as success instead of failure. the fix is trivial: change `sys.exit(0)` to `sys.exit(1)` at line 309 (or remove the error-path todo and update the exit code in the same step). (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

(flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

## Sprint 4 — §16.5 verbatim

**Goal.** Authorization layer (§6, §8) and `topic_status` (§7) ship. `consult_perspective` rewritten to actually clone. **Solo bot infrastructure pre-flighted in parallel** so S5 is pure code work.

This is a heavier sprint than earlier drafts implied — 19 read-phase tools plus read surfaces hiding in `write_tools.py` (`list_scheduled_tasks`, etc.) all get `scope` parameter changes, and tool-schema changes are model-behavior risk.

**Pre-flight context.**

- Lock decision A (peek window): default 14d. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision D (status cap N): default 5 most-recently-active topics per user. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision B: status update folded into `record` step, per §7.5. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision: which solo bot is #2 — coach, career topic, Discord transport. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision C (solo crisis default): refer to dyadic bot + external resources. ✓ Locked above.
- Read `consult_perspective.py:105-139` — the current code reconstructs `TurnContext` field-by-field, it does not clone. Plan a `dataclasses.replace` helper.
- Audit the read-phase tool registry (`tools/registry.py:157`) — count is ~19. Catalogue which need a `scope` arg vs which are scope-irrelevant (`get_bot_actions`, `recent_activity`, etc.).

**Work items, ordered (authorization track).**

1. `ReadScopes`/`WriteScopes` enforcement: every read tool consults `ctx.read_scopes`; every write consults `ctx.write_scopes`. Add `scope` parameter to artifact-reading tools only (skip scope-irrelevant tools). With one topic, `"own"` and `"all"` resolve the same — verify plumbing without changing output.
2. **`consult_perspective` rewrite**: replace the field-by-field `TurnContext` reconstruction at `consult_perspective.py:105` with a `dataclasses.replace(ctx, …)` helper. Add a unit test that enumerates every `TurnContext` field and asserts none are dropped on clone. Add a lint that fails if any new `TurnContext(...)` constructor appears outside the clone helper.
3. `set_topic_status` tool. Register only for `mediator` initially. Folded into `record` step instruction. Enforce headline ≤ 80 chars, body ≤ 300 chars.
4. Hot context: status block (own topic) for served user(s) + pair (`dyad_id` set, `user_id` NULL). Policy-gated cross-topic status injection — code path live but with one topic emits nothing.
5. Cross-topic peek block code path — same: code path live, emits nothing with one topic.
6. Mediator's BotSpec: `cross_topic_policy = "peek"`, `read_scopes = ReadScopes(topics={"own"}, allow_cross_topic_peek=True, allow_cross_topic_status_injection=True)`, `write_scopes = WriteScopes(topics={"relationship"}, require_reason_for_cross_topic=True)`.
7. Lint/test: every DB-touching function in `read_tools.py`/`write_tools.py` accepts and uses `ctx`.
8. **Tool-schema rollout strategy**: ship `scope` parameter undocumented in tool descriptions for one deploy, observe no behavior regression in evals, then surface in descriptions in a follow-up deploy. THIS SPRINT outputs the undocumented form.
9. Per-(user, bot) pause WRITE path (read path landed in S2a): admin endpoint + tool, defaulting to off.

**Work items, in parallel (solo pre-flight track) — STAGING ONLY.**

10. Provision the solo "coach" bot's transport in STAGING: new Discord bot account.
11. Create `channels`/`bots`/`topics`/`bot_bindings` rows for the solo bot in **staging only** — not prod yet. Add a migration if needed (e.g. `0031_coach_staging_seed.sql`); only applies to staging.
12. Configure webhook endpoint, secrets, provider allowlists for the new transport in staging.
13. (DEFER if blocked) Identify and obtain consent from the target user. Written expectations on what the bot does and doesn't do. — If you cannot identify the target user, write a placeholder TODO; do not block on it.
14. Transport-specific OOB guardrail test: send a known-bad message through the new transport in staging, verify OOB guardrail fires. — If staging is not reachable, write the test scaffold + skip; do not block.
15. Observability dashboards: confirm the per-bot split panes built in S2a render correctly for a second (staging-only) bot. — Code-level check is sufficient; do not require actual Grafana access.

**Mid-sprint checkpoint.**

- Mediator running with authorization wired. Pytest 534+ pass.
- A no-op second `BotSpec` in a test (`read_scopes.topics={"career"}`) fails to read `relationship` artifacts.
- Solo bot transport reachable in staging; webhook resolves to the right `bot_id`; OOB guardrail fires.

**Definition of done.**

- Every artifact read/write checks `ctx.read_scopes`/`ctx.write_scopes`. `consult_perspective` cloning verified by enumeration test.
- Mediator writes status; status block renders.
- Negative-permission test in CI passes.
- Solo bot transport, channel, secrets, consent are all green in staging (or explicit TODO if blocked).

**Risks.**

- `scope` parameter on every artifact-reading tool changes tool schemas → may affect mediator. The undocumented-first rollout strategy mitigates.
- Status injection token budget. Enforce headline ≤ 80, body ≤ 300 in `set_topic_status`.
- `consult_perspective` is the easiest leak path — the enumeration test is MANDATORY.
- Solo pre-flight runs in parallel; if it blocks (e.g. Discord bot account approval delays), defer those items to S5 with explicit TODOs but DON'T expand S5 by more than ~3 days.

**Deliberately not in this sprint.**

Multi-topic writes via `topic_slugs`. Solo bot prompt or hot context code (lands in S5). Account-linking workflow. PROD promotion of the solo bot (S5).

## S1-S3 lessons the executor must honor

1. **CLI scripts**: invoke with `--help` to confirm parseable.
2. **SQL fragments in Python strings**: dry-run via `EXPLAIN` or sanity-check types (no `max(uuid)` etc.).
3. **asyncpg pool against `DATABASE_URL`**: pass `statement_cache_size=0` (Supabase port 6543 is transaction-mode).
4. **No `hash()` for deterministic IDs** — use `hashlib.sha1`.
5. **Schema filters in validation queries** use `'mediator'` not `'public'`.
6. **For psql migrations against Supabase**: use port 5432 session-mode for DDL.
7. **Don't introduce scope creep**: no unrelated features or unused fields in shared classes.
8. **NO defensive fallbacks**: per S3 lesson, don't add `topic_id IS NULL` or similar permissive filters.
9. **For verify-human-heavy plans**: keep criterion count manageable (~10-15); each criterion should be cheaply auto-verifiable from artifacts.
10. **S3 cutover is committed**: every artifact read goes through `topic_filter.join_artifact_topics()`. New code follows this pattern, don't reintroduce direct reads.
11. **Pytest baseline**: 534 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on s3-join-cutover HEAD. S4 must maintain or improve.

- Any test that was passing on `s3-join-cutover` HEAD (commit 52d6dab) starts failing — STOP, report.
- `consult_perspective` enumeration test fails to enumerate any field — STOP, fix (this is a real correctness gap).
- Tool-schema changes break mediator behavior in eval (if eval suite available) — STOP, audit.
- Solo bot infra accidentally touches prod (any non-staging DB write) — STOP, revert.
- Negative-permission test (career-scoped bot trying to read relationship artifacts) PASSES (it should FAIL — that's the point) — STOP, fix authorization layer.

        Debt watch items (do not make these worse):
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan’s `scripts/seed_channels.py` uses `on conflict (transport, address, coalesce(guild_id,''), coalesce(channel_id,'')) do nothing`, but the 0020 migration defines the table with a standard `unique (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)` constraint on raw columns. postgresql `on conflict` target lists must reference the exact column names of a unique constraint or a matching unique index; expression constructs like `coalesce` in the target list do not match a raw-column unique constraint and will raise a syntax or 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the on conflict specification' error at runtime. the seed script will fail unless either (a) the table is changed to use an expression-based unique index with those exact coalesce expressions, or (b) the seed script is rewritten to query-first/insert-if-missing or uses the plain column names and accepts the null-handling semantics of the constraint. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: phase b cte pair (`ins` and `src`) requires identical where/order/limit clauses for cursor correctness. both are written aligned but nothing enforces the invariant during executor edits; drift would silently mis-advance cursor. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: step 5.1 says `dyad_id` is appended `before the existing-fields preserved block beginning at line 34`. actual line 34 in turn_context.py is a blank/comment line followed by `current_step: turnstep = "respond"` at the next line. placement intent is clear (append at end of optional block), but the line reference may drift after the field is added. minor precision wobble; not a blocker. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

## Orchestration

NOTE: `app/services/hot_context.py`, `app/services/prompts.py`, `app/services/time_context.py` were touched in S3 (allowed for read-rewrites) and committed. **Profile (locked).** `--profile premium --robustness standard --depth high`. Reason: this is THE apex sprint of the buildout — defines authorization contracts that S5+ will rely on. `consult_perspective` is the easiest leak path. Tool-schema changes are model-behavior risk. Opus 4.7 across all phases.

**Locked decisions (do not relitigate during plan/critique):**
1. **Peek window default**: 14 days. (§16.5 lock decision A.)
2. **Status cap N**: 5 most-recently-active topics per user. (§16.5 lock decision D.)

4. **Solo bot #2 identity**: "coach" — career/work coaching. Topic slug = `"career"`. Transport = Discord (parallel to mediator's). Provision in staging only; do NOT touch prod for the solo bot in S4. (§16.5 lock decision: which solo bot.)
5. **Solo crisis default**: refer to dyadic bot + external resources. (§16.5 lock decision C.)
6. **Tool-schema rollout**: ship `scope` parameter UNDOCUMENTED in tool descriptions for one deploy, observe no regression in evals, surface in descriptions in a FOLLOW-UP deploy (not in this sprint). Sprint outputs the undocumented form.
7. **`scope` parameter scope**: artifact-reading tools only. Skip scope-irrelevant tools (`get_bot_actions`, `recent_activity`, etc.).
8. **Solo bot infra in staging only**: do NOT promote to prod in S4. S5 owns the prod promotion.
9. **NO multi-topic writes**: that's S6. S4 ships the mechanism, S6 exercises it.

## Sprint 4 — §16.5 verbatim

**Goal.** Authorization layer (§6, §8) and `topic_status` (§7) ship. `consult_perspective` rewritten to actually clone. **Solo bot infrastructure pre-flighted in parallel** so S5 is pure code work.

This is a heavier sprint than earlier drafts implied — 19 read-phase tools plus read surfaces hiding in `write_tools.py` (`list_scheduled_tasks`, etc.) all get `scope` parameter changes, and tool-schema changes are model-behavior risk.

**Pre-flight context.**

- Lock decision A (peek window): default 14d. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision D (status cap N): default 5 most-recently-active topics per user. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision B: status update folded into `record` step, per §7.5. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision: which solo bot is #2 — coach, career topic, Discord transport. ✓ Locked above.
- Lock decision C (solo crisis default): refer to dyadic bot + external resources. ✓ Locked above.
- Read `consult_perspective.py:105-139` — the current code reconstructs `TurnContext` field-by-field, it does not clone. Plan a `dataclasses.replace` helper.
- Audit the read-phase tool registry (`tools/registry.py:157`) — count is ~19. Catalogue which need a `scope` arg vs which are scope-irrelevant (`get_bot_actions`, `recent_activity`, etc.).

**Work items, ordered (authorization track).**

1. `ReadScopes`/`WriteScopes` enforcement: every read tool consults `ctx.read_scopes`; every write consults `ctx.write_scopes`. Add `scope` parameter to artifact-reading tools only (skip scope-irrelevant tools). With one topic, `"own"` and `"all"` resolve the same — verify plumbing without changing output.
2. **`consult_perspective` rewrite**: replace the field-by-field `TurnContext` reconstruction at `consult_perspective.py:105` with a `dataclasses.replace(ctx, …)` helper. Add a unit test that enumerates every `TurnContext` field and asserts none are dropped on clone. Add a lint that fails if any new `TurnContext(...)` constructor appears outside the clone helper.
3. `set_topic_status` tool. Register only for `mediator` initially. Folded into `record` step instruction. Enforce headline ≤ 80 chars, body ≤ 300 chars.
4. Hot context: status block (own topic) for served user(s) + pair (`dyad_id` set, `user_id` NULL). Policy-gated cross-topic status injection — code path live but with one topic emits nothing.
5. Cross-topic peek block code path — same: code path live, emits nothing with one topic.
6. Mediator's BotSpec: `cross_topic_policy = "peek"`, `read_scopes = ReadScopes(topics={"own"}, allow_cross_topic_peek=True, allow_cross_topic_status_injection=True)`, `write_scopes = WriteScopes(topics={"relationship"}, require_reason_for_cross_topic=True)`.
7. Lint/test: every DB-touching function in `read_tools.py`/`write_tools.py` accepts and uses `ctx`.
8. **Tool-schema rollout strategy**: ship `scope` parameter undocumented in tool descriptions for one deploy, observe no behavior regression in evals, then surface in descriptions in a follow-up deploy. THIS SPRINT outputs the undocumented form.
9. Per-(user, bot) pause WRITE path (read path landed in S2a): admin endpoint + tool, defaulting to off.

**Work items, in parallel (solo pre-flight track) — STAGING ONLY.**

15. Observability dashboards: confirm the per-bot split panes built in S2a render correctly for a second (staging-only) bot. — Code-level check is sufficient; do not require actual Grafana access.

**Mid-sprint checkpoint.**

- Mediator running with authorization wired. Pytest 534+ pass.
- A no-op second `BotSpec` in a test (`read_scopes.topics={"career"}`) fails to read `relationship` artifacts.
- Solo bot transport reachable in staging; webhook resolves to the right `bot_id`; OOB guardrail fires.

**Definition of done.**

- Every artifact read/write checks `ctx.read_scopes`/`ctx.write_scopes`. `consult_perspective` cloning verified by enumeration test.
- Mediator writes status; status block renders.
- Negative-permission test in CI passes.
- Solo bot transport, channel, secrets, consent are all green in staging (or explicit TODO if blocked).

**Risks.**

- `scope` parameter on every artifact-reading tool changes tool schemas → may affect mediator. The undocumented-first rollout strategy mitigates.
- Status injection token budget. Enforce headline ≤ 80, body ≤ 300 in `set_topic_status`.
- `consult_perspective` is the easiest leak path — the enumeration test is MANDATORY.
- Solo pre-flight runs in parallel; if it blocks (e.g. Discord bot account approval delays), defer those items to S5 with explicit TODOs but DON'T expand S5 by more than ~3 days.

**Deliberately not in this sprint.**

Multi-topic writes via `topic_slugs`. Solo bot prompt or hot context code (lands in S5). Account-linking workflow. PROD promotion of the solo bot (S5).

## S1-S3 lessons the executor must honor

1. **CLI scripts**: invoke with `--help` to confirm parseable.
2. **SQL fragments in Python strings**: dry-run via `EXPLAIN` or sanity-check types (no `max(uuid)` etc.).
3. **asyncpg pool against `DATABASE_URL`**: pass `statement_cache_size=0` (Supabase port 6543 is transaction-mode).
4. **No `hash()` for deterministic IDs** — use `hashlib.sha1`.
5. **Schema filters in validation queries** use `'mediator'` not `'public'`.
6. **For psql migrations against Supabase**: use port 5432 session-mode for DDL.
7. **Don't introduce scope creep**: no unrelated features or unused fields in shared classes.
8. **NO defensive fallbacks**: per S3 lesson, don't add `topic_id IS NULL` or similar permissive filters.
9. **For verify-human-heavy plans**: keep criterion count manageable (~10-15); each criterion should be cheaply auto-verifiable from artifacts.
10. **S3 cutover is committed**: every artifact read goes through `topic_filter.join_artifact_topics()`. New code follows this pattern, don't reintroduce direct reads.
11. **Pytest baseline**: 534 pass / 0 fail / 3 skip on s3-join-cutover HEAD. S4 must maintain or improve.

        Debt watch items (do not make these worse):
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan’s `scripts/seed_channels.py` uses `on conflict (transport, address, coalesce(guild_id,''), coalesce(channel_id,'')) do nothing`, but the 0020 migration defines the table with a standard `unique (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)` constraint on raw columns. postgresql `on conflict` target lists must reference the exact column names of a unique constraint or a matching unique index; expression constructs like `coalesce` in the target list do not match a raw-column unique constraint and will raise a syntax or 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the on conflict specification' error at runtime. the seed script will fail unless either (a) the table is changed to use an expression-based unique index with those exact coalesce expressions, or (b) the seed script is rewritten to query-first/insert-if-missing or uses the plain column names and accepts the null-handling semantics of the constraint. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

        Debt watch items (do not make these worse):
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan’s `scripts/seed_channels.py` uses `on conflict (transport, address, coalesce(guild_id,''), coalesce(channel_id,'')) do nothing`, but the 0020 migration defines the table with a standard `unique (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)` constraint on raw columns. postgresql `on conflict` target lists must reference the exact column names of a unique constraint or a matching unique index; expression constructs like `coalesce` in the target list do not match a raw-column unique constraint and will raise a syntax or 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the on conflict specification' error at runtime. the seed script will fail unless either (a) the table is changed to use an expression-based unique index with those exact coalesce expressions, or (b) the seed script is rewritten to query-first/insert-if-missing or uses the plain column names and accepts the null-handling semantics of the constraint. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: phase b cte pair (`ins` and `src`) requires identical where/order/limit clauses for cursor correctness. both are written aligned but nothing enforces the invariant during executor edits; drift would silently mis-advance cursor. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)

  "content": "\"\"\"T30 throwaway: exercise the negative-permission scenario end-to-end.\n\nA coach-shaped TurnContext (read_scopes={'career'}, write_scopes={'career'},\nprimary_topic_slug='relationship') must:\n  1. fail to read relationship artifacts (get_memories returns is_error=True\n     with error.startswith('scope_denied'))\n  2. fail to write relationship artifacts (add_memory raises ToolCallRejected\n     with 'write_scope_denied' in the payload)\n\nIf either succeeds, that's the STOP condition: \"negative-permission test\nPASSES — it must FAIL — fix authorization layer\". This script asserts both.\n\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport asyncio\nfrom types import SimpleNamespace\nfrom uuid import uuid4\n\nfrom app.bots.base import ReadScopes, WriteScopes\nfrom app.services.tools.read_tools import get_memories\nfrom app.services.tools.write_tools import ToolCallRejected, add_memory\nfrom tool_schemas import AddMemoryInput, GetMemoriesInput, MemoryStatus\n\n\nasync def main() -> int:\n    coach_ctx = SimpleNamespace(\n        pool=None,\n        bot_id=\"coach\",\n        turn_id=uuid4(),\n        user=SimpleNamespace(id=uuid4()),\n        partner=SimpleNamespace(id=uuid4()),\n        primary_topic_id=uuid4(),\n        primary_topic_slug=\"relationship\",  # NB: relationship, not career\n        read_scopes=ReadScopes(topics=frozenset({\"career\"})),\n        write_scopes=WriteScopes(topics=frozenset({\"career\"})),\n    )\n\n    # Read denial\n    out = await get_memories(coach_ctx, GetMemoriesInput(scope=\"own\", status=MemoryStatus.active))\n    assert out.is_error is True, f\"FAIL: read should be denied but got is_error={out.is_error}\"\n    assert out.error and out.error.startswith(\"scope_denied\"), f\"FAIL: read error wrong: {out.error}\"\n    assert out.memories == [], f\"FAIL: empty memories shape: {out.memories}\"\n\n    # Write denial\n    try:\n        await add_memory(coach_ctx, AddMemoryInput(about_user_id=None, content=\"x\"))\n    except ToolCallRejected as exc:\n        err = exc.result.get(\"error\", \"\")\n        assert \"write_scope_denied\" in err, f\"FAIL: write error wrong: {err}\"\n    else:\n        raise AssertionError(\"FAIL: add_memory should have raised ToolCallRejected but did not\")\n\n    print(\"OK: coach-shaped ctx denied on BOTH read (get_memories) and write (add_memory). Negative-permission gate works.\")\n    return 0\n\n\nif __name__ == \"__main__\":\n    raise SystemExit(asyncio.run(main()))\n"
}

        Debt watch items (do not make these worse):
- [DEBT] are-the-proposed-changes-technically-correct: are the proposed changes technically correct?: the plan’s `scripts/seed_channels.py` uses `on conflict (transport, address, coalesce(guild_id,''), coalesce(channel_id,'')) do nothing`, but the 0020 migration defines the table with a standard `unique (transport, address, guild_id, channel_id)` constraint on raw columns. postgresql `on conflict` target lists must reference the exact column names of a unique constraint or a matching unique index; expression constructs like `coalesce` in the target list do not match a raw-column unique constraint and will raise a syntax or 'no unique or exclusion constraint matching the on conflict specification' error at runtime. the seed script will fail unless either (a) the table is changed to use an expression-based unique index with those exact coalesce expressions, or (b) the seed script is rewritten to query-first/insert-if-missing or uses the plain column names and accepts the null-handling semantics of the constraint. (flagged 1 times across 1 plans)
